studies.author_reported_summary: Dependent bacterial pairs generally adapted less than supplemented monocultures, with treatment-specific exceptions and escape to autonomy; coevolution benefits changed with supplementation.
studies.limits: Main comparison changes dependence, supplementation and community context together; 80 samples derive from 16 cultures split five ways. The authors do not support a universal weakest-link account and do not establish descendant collective reproduction.

studies.author_reported_summary: The Results report 37/48 and 41/48 surviving populations under two stresses, with rescue accompanied by loss of one detected partner and evolved autonomy; Methods and Figure 2c denominators remain unresolved.
studies.limits: Results, Methods and Figure 2c report non-reconciled sample counts. Population survival is not partnership preservation; proposed biochemical flux routes were not all directly measured, and no collective reproductive assay was performed.

studies.author_reported_summary: An evolved resource-use innovation in one historical LTEE population generated cross-feeding opportunities; producer presence reversed the relative fitness benefit of an evolved consumer phenotype.
studies.limits: One historical Ara−3 lineage; chemical time courses use one culture per clone and Figure 6 symbol labels conflict with the Results. Cross-feeding is not necessarily reciprocal mutualism, and no daughter collective reconstruction is demonstrated.
